title.narrative: Food assistance to people affected by EL Nino induced drought

description.narrative: Lesotho’s food security situation remains dire due to El Nino induced dry spells in 2023/2024 rainy season. The IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis projects that 403,000 people in rural areas will be in crisis or worse (IPC3+) from October 2024 to March 2025 while in urban areas, the Economic Capacity of Households to Meet Essential Needs indicates that more than 296,000 people will be food insecure. The total food-insecure population is estimated at 700,000 for the 2024/25 consumption year which is an increase of 17 percent from last year. All 10 districts of Lesotho are anticipated to be in IPC 3 (Crisis) or worse from October 2024 to March 2025 with Berea, Mafeteng, Maseru, Mohale’s hoek, Qacha’s Nek and Quthing, recording the highest percentage of people in need of humanitarian assistance. Five percent of the population in four (Maseru, Mohale’s Hoek, Qacha’s Nek, Quthing) of the six most affected districts is in IPC 4 and have highest survival deficit food gap that ranges from 15 to over 50 percent. WFP plans to prioritize support to 272,000 people (with estimated budget of USD 45,861,498) in rural areas of the six most hard-hit districts (Qacha’s Nek, Maseru, Mohale`s Hoek, Quthing, Berea and Thaba-Tseka) for a period of six months (October 2024 to March 2025) that also happens to be the lean season period when majority of households have depleted their harvested food stock. The six targeted districts are the most adversely affected with 25 to 40 percent of the rural population in IPC 3-crisis while five percent of the population in four of the six targeted districts is in IPC 4 and have highest survival deficit food gap that ranges from 15 to over 50 percent. Based on the 2024 Lesotho Vulnerability Assessment report, WFP will target the poor and very poor households. Subject to availability of resources, the assistance will further be extended to 213,000 food insecure people in urban areas of the six prioritized districts, with the estimated additional resource requirements of USD 43,584,565. Through the CERF funding, WFP plans to assist 15,174 people (out of the 272,000 targeted) for a period of three months (October 2024-December 2024), targeting the rural areas of the most hard hit four districts in which five percent of the population is in IPC 4. Of the targeted 15,174 people, a total of 9,104 people from hard-to-reach areas will receive commodity voucher assistance while a total of 6,070 people from accessible areas within the targeted districts will receive unconditional cash assistance. The voucher assistance will be administered through a network of local retailers to provide the prescribed food assistance to the targeted people. The cash transfers will be administered through the Standard Lesotho Bank UNAYO platform.The transfer modality is informed by the transfer modality and mechanism feasibility assessments including beneficiary preferences, security, and protection aspects. The transfer value will be equivalent to USD 88.00 per household or USD 22.00 per person per month. The transfer value is calculated based on the bare minimum requirements for survival (Survival Threshold) used by Lesotho Vulnerability Assessment Committee and this includes; (i) minimum food needs - 2100 Kilocalories/day – Maize meal/grain (carbohydrates), Beans/pulses (Protein), Oil (Fat), Vegetables (minerals and vitamins), and salt (iodine). WFP mainstreams nutrition across its programmes and will secure partnership with nutrition actors for effective dissemination of protection, gender and nutrition messages during the intervention period. The nutrition messaging will be intensified through bulk messaging as well as community-based approaches. In case of commodity voucher transfer modality, diverse food basket will be provided, and the nutrition education will influence adoption and consumption of nutritious food.
